why: Closes our biggest QA hole (a 2 s freeze passes stills review) and is pure ffmpeg + Node, so it fits the deterministic-frames bar.
note: `forensics` implements still holds, pops, one-frame flashes, ghost frames, judder (repeats + irregular pts), banding, loop seam, hard-cut shot lengths, declared-intent qa.json, flagged contact strip. Self-test on B and C drafts found real still holds and a slow open; banding is a heuristic score, judder near-stalls are pointers only.

why: We already used a fresh reviewer; the verification-round template and regression hunt are cheap and catch real regressions.
note: Verification rounds (FIXED/PARTLY/STILL PRESENT, at most 3 fixes, dense windows), ledger table in review.md, one-round-after-gates then ask, hard stop at 6. Builder passes only the previous defect list.

why: The cap on full-frame beat hits is a hard, checkable rule; the least-squares beat-grid fit belongs to sound-design, not review.
note: Landed: sync reports full-frame hit count (max 3) and min gap in beats (16, via --bpm), loop seam in forensics, rubric line. Deferred to prompts/50 and audio.md owners: beat-grid fit, half/double-time check, band-classified onsets.

why: Numbers give reviews something to check, but the source films are unnamed, so they are reference points, not gates.
note: Pacing norms in rubric as reading points; forensics supplies the numbers (median shot, still share, hard cuts). Explicitly not pass/fail, except the spent-once stillness rule.

why: Optical-flow check catches surges and stops that stills cannot show; the speed-table brief format is a motion-doc matter.
note: `flow` = global affine Lucas-Kanade pyramid on a 30 fps copy, speed in frame widths/s incl. zoom, speed dips, zoom reversals, plot. Verified on synthetic pan-with-stall (dip found at 2.03-3.03 s, truth 2-3 s) and zoom reversal (found at 3.03 s, truth 3.0 s). Not a real-camera test beyond the two drafts; local type animation is skipped as non-camera. Speed-table format for briefs left to the motion-studio/director docs.

why: Plotting value and velocity before changing code beats guessing, and costs seconds.
note: `plot` takes JSON/CSV in several shapes, --deriv adds velocity and flags zero-velocity stretches mid-curve. Studio-side exporter helper and prompt 15 step belong to the studio/prompts owners.

why: Scoring against an exemplar tells the builder how ours falls short, which a vacuum score cannot.
note: `compare` accepts an image, a contact sheet (--cols/--rows) or a video, matched times, reference row over ours, per-pair palette/luma hint; rubric asks for one gap line per pair and forbids copying the reference look.

why: The critics' warning is more useful than the list: even rhythm is the AI-motion tell, so variance is reviewed.
note: Pacing and tension variance section and checklist: name the hard cut and the fast fade, same duration everywhere flagged, one easing everywhere flagged; crossfade-everything and one-easing-everywhere rejected as rules.

why: Reviewing against stated, measurable criteria is cheap; writing the glossary belongs to the brief template.
note: Reviewer now checks glossary/acceptance criteria by number and flags undefined vague words. Brief template glossary block and revision prompt output owned by others.

why: A pre-build plan critic is a builder step and sits in the build prompts, not the post-render reviewer.
note: No reviewer change; the optional fresh critic can reuse agent.md's spawn pattern. Belongs in prompts/12 and 14 and phases.md.

why: Only its cheap-tells catalogue is review material; the concept triple is a direction matter.
note: Borrowed tells into banned-effects check (borrowed props, demo with no cause, recycled end card, device dropping at a seam).

why: Selected rework-derived rules are cheap pre-empting checks; the rest are taste rules for build docs.
note: Added checks: wordmark hold under 1 s, one sheen per hero, handheld shake, last-beat disclaimer 2.5 s.
